title: Forensic Pathology Fellowship
inst: University of New Mexico Office of the Medical Investigator (OMI)
Department: Office of the Medical Investigator (statewide death investigation system, UNM School of Medicine)
Deadline: Currently accepting applications for the 2028-2029 fellowship year via ERAS; interviews begin September 2026
Eligibility: Completion of AP-only or combined AP/CP training in an ACGME-accredited residency by the start of the fellowship
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (listed in ERAS forensic pathology participating programmes)
Application method: ERAS; participates in the Match (applicants must register for the Match)
Summary: A one-year forensic pathology fellowship at New Mexico's statewide Office of the Medical Investigator with high autopsy volume, routine postmortem CT/MRI and rotations in toxicology, odontology, anthropology and crime labs.

title: Hematopathology Fellowship
inst: University of New Mexico School of Medicine
Deadline: For best consideration apply by December for the fellowship year beginning two years later (e.g. December 2024 for 2026-27)
Eligibility: Graduates meet American Board of Pathology hematopathology certification eligibility; CAP standardized application, CV and personal statement
Application method: CAP Standardized Application for Pathology Fellowship emailed to the programme; participates in the Match (Society for Hematopathology fellowship match)
Summary: A hematopathology fellowship based at TriCore Reference Laboratories integrating morphology with 10-colour flow cytometry, cytogenetics and in-house NGS, with graduated responsibility including national consultation cases.

title: Molecular Genetic Pathology Fellowship
inst: University of New Mexico School of Medicine
Deadline: For best consideration apply by February for the subsequent academic year (e.g. February 2026 for 2027-2028)
Eligibility: MD plus residency training in pathology or medical genetics in an ACGME-accredited programme; CAP application, CV, personal statement and three letters (one from the programme director)
Application method: CAP standardized application; participates in the Match (Association for Molecular Pathology guidance)
Summary: An ACGME-accredited MGP fellowship with UNM and TriCore Reference Laboratories covering molecular oncology, HLA typing, hereditary genetic testing, molecular microbiology and cytogenetics/FISH, plus genetics clinics.

title: Blood Banking/Transfusion Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of New Mexico School of Medicine
Summary: A blood banking and transfusion medicine fellowship covering UNM Hospital, UNM Cancer Center and Sandoval Regional Medical Center transfusion services, with apheresis, tissue bank and hemoglobinopathy exposure.

title: Cytopathology Fellowship
inst: University of New Mexico School of Medicine
Eligibility: Graduates are eligible for American Board of Pathology cytopathology subspecialty certification
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited cytopathology fellowship with palpation- and ultrasound-guided FNA training, about 70,000 Pap and 7,500 non-gynaecologic samples annually and a laboratory management rotation at TriCore.

title: Surgical Pathology Fellowship
inst: University of New Mexico School of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of a 4-year AP/CP or 3-year AP-only ACGME-accredited pathology residency; US citizenship or permanent residency (green card) required
International applicants: Not eligible unless US citizen or permanent resident (programme page)
Application method: CAP Standardized Fellowship Application Form; virtual interviews for selected candidates
Visa support: None - US citizenship or permanent residency required (programme page)
Licence requirement: Full New Mexico medical licence required
Summary: A one-year practice-level surgical pathology fellowship at New Mexico's only academic medical center, with frozen sections, consult review and junior-attending sign-out in the second half of the year.
